As a large, global financial institution, Citi faces particularly complex

provenance:
HELD-OUT, FROZEN AT AUTHORING 2026-08-26 (D6) — labels written and committed BEFORE the first run, per evals/heldout/README.md. Citigroup Inc. FY2025 10-K, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000083100126000011/c-20251231.htm, accession 0000831001-26-000011, filed 2026-02-20, period end 2025-12-31, 16,150,764 bytes, iXBRL — the largest file in either set. WHY THIS FILING: it is the second of the two filings that failed live at the 2026-08-24 demo (docs/evals/audits/2026-08-25-demo-intel-citi-postmortem.md), Citigroup appears in NO fixture, golden, adversarial or held-out case anywhere in this repo, and it is the money-center-bank class the postmortem §4 ranks first among known-difficult filers. It is also the most recent Citigroup 10-K on EDGAR — the only 10-K in the CIK 831001 recent-submissions window — so it is exactly what a user tries today.

VERIFICATION. Independent tag-strip regex scan (tags -> single space, entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed; imports NOTHING from src/) plus raw-byte greps for every character-level claim. The extractor has never been invoked on this file. Scan size 1,507,550 chars from 16,150,764 raw bytes; the first ~348,000 scan chars are the iXBRL hidden-fact block, and the cover begins after it.

STRUCTURAL FINDING (a hypothesis at paragraph granularity until a run tests it) AND ITS CHARACTER-LEVEL BACKING (read from raw bytes, so claimed): this filing contains ZERO occurrences of the string 'Item <digit>' naming a 10-K item code. Raw-byte counts in the 16,150,764-byte file: 'Item 1.' 0x, 'Item 1A' 0x, 'Item 7' 0x, 'Item 8' 0x, 'ITEM ' (uppercase) 0x. A case-insensitive raw regex for item-plus-digit returns exactly four hits in the whole file, and none is a 10-K heading: the cover's combined pointer 'Items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 of Part III' (raw offset 1,828,047), two Regulation S-K citations ('Item 402(v)' at 1,859,455 and 'Item 408' at 15,875,549), and one 'Reconciling Items' phrase. The document maps itself to the SEC form via a 'FORM 10-K CROSS-REFERENCE INDEX' (scan offset 352,469, raw-byte count 1x) whose rows are BARE codes with no 'Item' prefix — '1. Business 4-36, 121-127, 129, 160-164, 299-300', '1A. Risk Factors 49-62', '1B. Unresolved Staff Comments Not Applicable', and so on. That is the axp-2008 bare-code shape (evals/fixtures/axp-2008), on a filing that carries it for EVERY item rather than for four.

The index lists 22 codes: 1, 1A, 1B, 1C, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7A, 8, 9, 9A, 9B, 9C, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. Item 16 (Form 10-K Summary, optional) is absent from it. Items 10-14 are answered by the cover sentence plus five asterisk footnotes pointing into the 2026 proxy statement. Not Applicable per the index: 1B, 2, 4, 9, 9C.

COVER DATE — AND A TRAP AVOIDED. The scan renders the cover as 'For the fiscal year ended December 31 , 2025', i.e. with the pgr-2023 'floating comma'. THAT IS A SCAN ARTIFACT AND IS NOT CLAIMED. The raw bytes read 'For the fiscal year ended <ix:nonNumeric ...>December 31</ix:nonNumeric>, 2025' — the space is a tag boundary the scan turns into a character, exactly the instrument failure the README's authoring-discipline section records for pgr-2023. Raw-byte counts: 'December 31, 2025' 159x, 'December 31 , 2025' 0x. Period end is 2025-12-31 and there is no floating comma.

ANCHORS, raw-byte counts in the whole file: 'As a large, global financial institution, Citi faces particularly complex' 1x — the second sentence of the RISK FACTORS section, scan offset ~503,000; 'DISCLOSURE CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES' 2x (the contents page and the body heading at scan 833,976, which is Item 9A territory, so it is the bleed tripwire for item 1A).

LENGTH FLOORS, measured from the scan with wide margins so they cannot encode the scan's known disagreement with the normalizer. RISK FACTORS is a single contiguous section the index maps 1:1 to Item 1A: scan 502,951 to 587,719 ('SUSTAINABILITY'), ~84,800 chars, floored at 20,000. CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS through the notes runs scan ~855,700 to ~1,435,500 ('FINANCIAL DATA SUPPLEMENT'), ~580,000 chars, and the index maps Item 8 to exactly that page range (134-298), floored at 100,000. Items 1 and 7 are floored at a deliberately LOOSE 2,000 because the index maps each to several DISCONTIGUOUS page ranges, so no single span is demonstrably the right answer; 2,000 is the postmortem §5 figure for the cheapest instrument that catches a stub collapse.

WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT. (a) A status for item 16 — the index omits it entirely, so `omitted` is the natural reading, but that is an enum judgment about the contract rather than a statement the document makes, and the csco-2016 precedent declined exactly this shape of negative after H1 caught it being wrong on xom-2021. It rides in expected_set_complete, which accepts any valid status. (b) Statuses for 1B, 2, 4, 9, 9C ('Not Applicable' per the index) for the same reason. (c) `incorporated_by_reference` on 10-14: the pointer is on the COVER and in index footnotes, not in any item body — how the pipeline ought to resolve that is a design question D9/D11 own, not ground truth. (d) `deterministic` — omitted on purpose, and this is the ONLY check csco-2016's shape carries that this case drops: at 16.1 MB it would double the run cost of the single most expensive case in the repo, and determinism is already pinned by every other case in the suite. (e) Any max_chars, any confidence value, anything about the iXBRL hidden-fact block.

PREDICTION, FROZEN BEFORE THE FIRST RUN so it cannot be retrofitted, and NOT asserted as a check. THIS CASE IS EXPECTED TO FAIL; that is the recorded outcome of D6, not a defect to fix here (the fixes are D8/D9/D11). Because the raw bytes carry no 'Item N' string at all, I expect NO heading candidates to be generated anywhere in the document, hence all 23 era items reported `missing` with null offsets at BASE_MISSING 0.40, `expected_items_mostly_missing` firing, and doc_status `ambiguous`. That is the LOW-confidence face of the D8 sensor problem (postmortem §8: unmatched headings land 0.40, headings matched to the wrong instances land 0.95) — the opposite face from intc-2025, which is why the two filings together are worth more than either alone. NOTE THE TENSION AND THAT I AM NOT RESOLVING IT: the demo reported per-item `conf 0.95` on Citigroup, which my structural reading does not predict; either the demo ran a different Citigroup document, or a heading path I cannot see from a tag-strip scan produces candidates anyway. The run settles it; I am recording the disagreement rather than assuming my scan wins.

BURN RULE: the moment this case's outcome influences implementation — a fix, a threshold, a declined fix documented with its outcome in hand, or a new case authored from it — it moves to evals/adversarial/ and is replaced. D11 must pass this filing WITHOUT ever having trained on it; the dev-side proxies for the pointer class are cvx-2015 and jpm-2024, both already in the dev set.
